claims.text: The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is as-cast and coarse-grained.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The reported 13.5% terminal strain of HfZrTiTa0.53 can be used as its baseline uniform tensile elongation.
Approximately 8–10% cold rolling followed immediately by recrystallization annealing will refine the grain structure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
The treatment can produce full recrystallization without excessive grain coarsening.
The processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will have a uniform fine-grained microstructure with a mean grain size near or below 1 μm.
Grain refinement will increase strain hardening and dislocation mobility in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Additional grain boundaries will impede crack initiation and propagation.
The refined, recrystallized structure will produce a more uniform deformation field and improve resistance to localized necking.
The proposed treatment will increase tensile ductility and uniform elongation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Uniform tensile elongation will increase by at least approximately 5 percentage points over a 13.5% baseline.
The processed alloy will retain a yield strength within ±5% of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has demonstrated impact-triggered chemical-energy release.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will preserve comparable impact-triggered energy release.
The expected tensile benefit applies at room temperature under quasi-static loading near 10^-3 s^-1.
The hypothesis does not extend the predicted benefit to elevated or cryogenic temperatures or to extreme strain rates.
Rolling and heat treatment produced a fine-grained CoCrNiV alloy with 1060 MPa yield strength and 24.1% uniform elongation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis alternates between calling 13.5% a terminal strain and treating it as a baseline uniform tensile elongation. Terminal strain, uniform tensile elongation, and total elongation are not interchangeable measures.
The baseline asserts demonstrated impact-triggered energy release for HfZrTiTa0.53, but no quantitative HfZrTiTa0.53 impact-energy baseline is supplied for the proposed comparison.
